- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction after peak.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- In multi-event periods (e.g., 20+ auctions), model overfits to recent trend; use 18-day history as anchor, not 30-day trend.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility — add ±1–2% volatility buffer around forecast.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak, price drops >10%), model overreacts — apply decay factor to forecast slope.
- In high-event periods with net supply negative, model tends to ignore event impact — explicitly reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per event if supply net > -30.
